title: Pearl's Happy Hums
markdown:
The meadow hummed with sunshine and smelled like sweet flowers. Pearl the piglet loved her quiet hums. She nudged a fluffy dandelion. It tickled her nose, and she giggled into a small hmm-mm-mmm that barely stirred the seeds.

Greta the goat trotted over. “What’s that happy tune, Pearl?”

“Just my hums,” Pearl whispered. “They’re so quiet, Greta. Not grand.”

Auntie Honoria, a fancy goose, swooshed in with her Goose Choir. They were practising for the Meadow Music Festival. “We need the most wonderful opening note ever,” Auntie Honoria boomed.

Pearl’s tummy felt fluttery. Her quiet hums seemed so tiny next to the geese’s loud honks. She tucked her snout toward the grass.

The choir lined up. “One, two, three,” Auntie Honoria called. Big honks filled the air. Then a surprise: tiny soft hums wove in. Pearl had hummed along without thinking. Greta added a happy bleat. Gran Ada the hen gave a soft cluck.

Auntie Honoria paused. “My, my. What are these lovely little sounds?” The little geese giggled. “They sound like happy fireflies.”

Auntie Honoria looked at Pearl. “Your hums are lovely. They’re your own special sound.” Pearl’s tummy stopped its flutter. A warm feeling spread. Maybe her hums were all right.

The next day Auntie Honoria called across the meadow. “Pearl, will you sing the grand opening note?”

Pearl’s snout wiggled. “Oh, Auntie, my voice is so tiny. Like a lost button.” She felt wobbly.

Greta nudged her. “Your little button hums are pretty and brave. Gran Ada says even small sounds can be strong.”

Pearl looked at Greta’s kind eyes. The festival was almost here. She wanted to share her hums.

On festival day the sun shone golden. Auntie Honoria smiled. “Ready, little hummer?”

Pearl nodded. Greta gave a thumbs-up. Gran Ada winked. Pearl imagined her hums like warm lanterns.

Auntie Honoria signaled. The geese honked their big beautiful sound. Pearl took a deep breath. The air smelled sweet. The grass felt cool. She thought of the tickly dandelion and Greta’s happy bleat.

Then she let out her sound. It was not a loud honk. It was a clear warm little hum, soft but steady, like a stream over pebbles. It floated and blended with the honks.

For a breath the meadow held still. A bee hung in the light. A dandelion clock forgot to blow. Then came gentle applause, like rustling leaves.

Auntie Honoria beamed. “Pearl, that was perfect. Your voice is like sunshine.”

Pearl felt a warm glow. She was not the loudest. She was the clearest. She was herself.

Later, as the sky painted itself with colours, Pearl sat with Greta and Gran Ada. She hummed a happy tune, a little louder this time. The hums felt full. They were not lost buttons anymore. They were brave happy sounds, made just for her to share.
characters: Pearl (quiet-hum piglet), Greta (kind meadow goat), Gran Ada (soft-cluck hen)
